title: Westminster Larger Catechism
snippet: 196 questions and answers expanding the Westminster doctrine for further study.

title: Westminster Larger Catechism — Q. 1
snippet: What is the chief and highest end of man?
body: Man's chief and highest end is to glorify God, and fully to enjoy him for ever.

title: Westminster Larger Catechism — Q. 2
snippet: How doth it appear that there is a God?
body: The very light of nature in man, and the works of God, declare plainly that there is a God; but his Word and Spirit only, do sufficiently and effectually reveal him unto men for their salvation.

title: Westminster Larger Catechism — Q. 3
snippet: What is the Word of God?
body: The Holy Scriptures of the Old and New Testaments are the Word of God, the only rule of faith and obedience.

title: Westminster Larger Catechism — Q. 4
snippet: How doth it appear that the Scriptures are the Word of God?
body: The Scriptures manifest themselves to be the Word of God, by their majesty and purity; by the consent of all the parts, and the scope of the whole, which is to give all glory to God; by their light and power to convince and convert sinners, to comfort and build up believers unto …

title: Westminster Larger Catechism — Q. 5
snippet: What do the Scriptures principally teach?
body: The Scriptures principally teach, what man is to believe concerning God, and what duty God requires of man.

title: Westminster Larger Catechism — Q. 6
snippet: What do the Scriptures make known of God?
body: The Scriptures make known what God is, the persons in the Godhead, his decrees, and the execution of his decrees.

title: Westminster Larger Catechism — Q. 7
snippet: What is God?
body: God is a Spirit, in and of himself infinite in being, glory, blessedness, and perfection; all-sufficient, eternal, unchangeable, incomprehensible, everywhere present, almighty, knowing all things, most wise, most holy, most just, most merciful and gracious, long-suffering, and ab…

title: Westminster Larger Catechism — Q. 8
snippet: Are there more Gods than one?
body: There is but one only, the living and true God.

title: Westminster Larger Catechism — Q. 9
snippet: How many persons are there in the Godhead?
body: There be three persons in the Godhead, the Father, the Son, and the Holy Ghost: and these three are one true, eternal God, the same in substance, equal in power and glory; although distinguished by their personal properties.

title: Westminster Larger Catechism — Q. 10
snippet: What are the personal properties of the three persons in the Godhead?
body: It is proper to the Father to beget the Son, and to the Son to be begotten of the Father, and to the Holy Ghost to proceed from the Father and the Son from all eternity.

title: Westminster Larger Catechism — Q. 11
snippet: How doth it appear that the Son and the Holy Ghost are God equal with the Father?
body: The Scriptures manifest that the Son and the Holy Ghost are God equal with the Father, ascribing unto them such names, attributes, works, and worship, as are proper to God only.

title: Westminster Larger Catechism — Q. 12
snippet: What are the decrees of God?
body: God's decrees are the wise, free, and holy acts of the counsel of his will, whereby, from all eternity, he hath, for his own glory, unchangeably fore-ordained whatsoever comes to pass in time, especially concerning angels and men.

title: Westminster Larger Catechism — Q. 13
snippet: What hath God especially decreed concerning angels and men?
body: God, by an eternal and immutable decree, out of his mere love, for the praise of his glorious grace, to be manifested in due time, hath elected some angels to glory; and in Christ hath chosen some men to eternal life, and the means thereof: and also according to his sovereign pow…

title: Westminster Larger Catechism — Q. 14
snippet: How doth God execute his decrees?
body: God executeth his decrees in the works of creation and providence, according to his infallible fore-knowledge, and the free and immutable counsel of his own will.

title: Westminster Larger Catechism — Q. 15
snippet: What is the work of creation?
body: The work of creation is that wherein God did in the beginning, by the word of his power, make of nothing the world, and all things therein, for himself, within the space of six days, and all very good.

title: Westminster Larger Catechism — Q. 16
snippet: How did God create angels?
body: God created all the angels spirits, immortal, holy, excelling in knowledge, mighty in power, to execute his commandments, and to praise his name, yet subject to change.

title: Westminster Larger Catechism — Q. 17
snippet: How did God create man?
body: After God had made all other creatures, he created man, male and female; formed the body of the man of the dust of the ground, and the woman of the rib of the man; endued them with living, reasonable, and immortal souls; made them after his own image, in knowledge, righteousness …

title: Westminster Larger Catechism — Q. 18
snippet: What are God's works of providence?
body: God's works of providence are his most holy, wise, and powerful preserving, and governing all his creatures; ordering them, and all their actions, to his own glory.

title: Westminster Larger Catechism — Q. 19
snippet: What is God's providence toward the angels?
body: God by his providence permitted some of the angels, willfully and irrecoverably, to fall into sin and damnation, limiting and ordering that, and all their sins, to his own glory; and established the rest in holiness and happiness; employing them all, at his pleasure, in the admin…

title: Westminster Larger Catechism — Q. 20
snippet: What was the providence of God toward man in the estate in which he was created?
body: The providence of God toward man in the estate in which he was created, was the placing him in paradise, appointing him to dress it, giving him liberty to eat of the fruit of the earth; putting the creatures under his dominion, and ordaining marriage for his help; affording him c…

title: Westminster Larger Catechism — Q. 21
snippet: Did man continue in that estate wherein God at first created him?
body: Our first parents being left to the freedom of their own will, through the temptation of Satan, transgressed the commandment of God, in eating the forbidden fruit, and thereby fell from the estate of innocency wherein they were created.

title: Westminster Larger Catechism — Q. 22
snippet: Did all mankind fall in that first transgression?
body: The covenant being made with Adam, as a public person, not for himself only, but for his posterity; all mankind descending from him by ordinary generation, sinned in him, and fell with him in that first transgression.

title: Westminster Larger Catechism — Q. 23
snippet: Into what estate did the fall bring mankind?
body: The fall brought mankind into an estate of sin and misery.

title: Westminster Larger Catechism — Q. 24
snippet: What is sin?
body: Sin is any want of conformity unto, or transgression of, any law of God, given as a rule to the reasonable creature.

title: Westminster Larger Catechism — Q. 25
snippet: Wherein consisteth the sinfulness of that estate whereinto man fell?
body: The sinfulness of that estate whereinto man fell, consisteth in the guilt of Adam's first sin, the want of that righteousness wherein he was created, and the corruption of his nature, whereby he is utterly indisposed, disabled, and made opposite unto all that is spiritually good,…

title: Westminster Larger Catechism — Q. 26
snippet: How is original sin conveyed from our first parents unto their posterity?
body: Original sin is conveyed from our first parents unto their posterity by natural generation, so as all that proceed from them in that way are conceived and born in sin.

title: Westminster Larger Catechism — Q. 27
snippet: What misery did the fall bring upon mankind?
body: The fall brought upon mankind the loss of communion with God, his displeasure and curse; so as we are by nature children of wrath, bond slaves to Satan, and justly liable to all punishments in this world and that which is to come.

title: Westminster Larger Catechism — Q. 28
snippet: What are the punishments of sin in this world?
body: The punishments of sin in this world, are either inward, as blindness of mind, a reprobate sense, strong delusions, hardness of heart, horror of conscience, and vile affections: or outward, as the curse of God upon the creatures for our sake; and all other evils that befall us in…

title: Westminster Larger Catechism — Q. 29
snippet: What are the punishments of sin in the world to come?
body: The punishments of sin in the world to come, are everlasting separation from the comfortable presence of God, and most grievous torments in soul and body, without intermission, in hell-fire for ever.

title: Westminster Larger Catechism — Q. 30
snippet: Doth God leave all mankind to perish in the estate of sin and misery?
body: God doth not leave all men to perish in the estate of sin and misery, into which they fell by the breach of the first covenant, commonly called the Covenant of Works; but of his mere love and mercy delivereth his elect out of it, and bringeth them into an estate of salvation by t…

title: Westminster Larger Catechism — Q. 31
snippet: With whom was the covenant of grace made?
body: The covenant of grace was made with Christ as the second Adam, and in him with all the elect as his seed.

title: Westminster Larger Catechism — Q. 32
snippet: How is the grace of God manifested in the second covenant?
body: The grace of God is manifested in the second covenant, in that he freely provideth and offereth to sinners a Mediator, and life and salvation by him; and, requiring faith as the condition to interest them in him, promiseth and giveth his Holy Spirit to all his elect, to work in t…

title: Westminster Larger Catechism — Q. 33
snippet: Was the covenant of grace always administered after one and the same manner?
body: The covenant of grace was not always administered after the same manner, but the administrations of it under the Old Testament were different from those under the New.

title: Westminster Larger Catechism — Q. 34
snippet: How was the covenant of grace administered under the Old Testament?
body: The covenant of grace was administered under the Old Testament, by promises, prophecies, sacrifices, circumcision, the passover, and other types and ordinances, which did all fore-signify Christ then to come, and were for that time sufficient to build up the elect in faith in the…

title: Westminster Larger Catechism — Q. 35
snippet: How is the covenant of grace administered under the New Testament?
body: Under the New Testament, when Christ the substance was exhibited, the same covenant of grace was and still is to be administered in the preaching of the Word, and the administration of the sacraments of baptism and the Lord's supper; in which grace and salvation are held forth in…

title: Westminster Larger Catechism — Q. 36
snippet: Who is the Mediator of the covenant of grace?
body: The only Mediator of the covenant of grace is the Lord Jesus Christ, who, being the eternal Son of God, of one substance and equal with the Father, in the fullness of time became man, and so was and continues to be God and man, in two entire distinct natures, and one person, fore…

title: Westminster Larger Catechism — Q. 37
snippet: How did Christ, being the Son of God, become man?
body: Christ the Son of God became man, by taking to himself a true body, and a reasonable soul, being conceived by the power of the Holy Ghost in the womb of the Virgin Mary, of her substance, and born of her, yet without sin.

title: Westminster Larger Catechism — Q. 38
snippet: Why was it requisite that the Mediator should be God?
body: It was requisite that the Mediator should be God, that he might sustain and keep the human nature from sinking under the infinite wrath of God, and the power of death; give worth and efficacy to his sufferings, obedience and intercession; and to satisfy God's justice, procure his…

title: Westminster Larger Catechism — Q. 39
snippet: Why was it requisite that the Mediator should be man?
body: It was requisite that the Mediator should be man, that he might advance our nature, perform obedience to the law, suffer and make intercession for us in our nature, have a fellow-feeling of our infirmities; that we might receive the adoption of sons, and have comfort and access w…

title: Westminster Larger Catechism — Q. 40
snippet: Why was it requisite that the Mediator should be God and man in one person?
body: It was requisite that the Mediator, who was to reconcile God and man, should himself be both God and man, and this in one person, that the proper works of each nature might be accepted of God for us, and relied on by us, as the works of the whole person.

title: Westminster Larger Catechism — Q. 41
snippet: Why was our Mediator called Jesus?
body: Our Mediator was called Jesus, because he saveth his people from their sins.

title: Westminster Larger Catechism — Q. 42
snippet: Why was our Mediator called Christ?
body: Our Mediator was called Christ, because he was anointed with the Holy Ghost above measure; and so set apart, and fully furnished with all authority and ability, to execute the offices of prophet, priest, and king of his Church, in the estate both of his humiliation and exaltation…

title: Westminster Larger Catechism — Q. 43
snippet: How doth Christ execute the office of a prophet?
body: Christ executeth the office of a prophet, in his revealing to the Church in all ages, by his Spirit and Word, in divers ways of administration, the whole will of God, in all things concerning their edification and salvation.

title: Westminster Larger Catechism — Q. 44
snippet: How doth Christ execute the office of a priest?
body: Christ executeth the office of a priest, in his once offering himself a sacrifice without spot to God, to be a reconciliation for the sins of his people; and in making continual intercession for them.

title: Westminster Larger Catechism — Q. 45
snippet: How doth Christ execute the office of a king?
body: Christ executeth the office of a king, in calling out of the world a people to himself, and giving them officers, laws, and censures, by which he visibly governs them; in bestowing saving grace upon his elect, rewarding their obedience, and correcting them for their sins, preserv…

title: Westminster Larger Catechism — Q. 46
snippet: What was the estate of Christ's humiliation?
body: The estate of Christ's humiliation was that low condition, wherein he, for our sakes, emptying himself of his glory, took upon him the form of a servant, in his conception and birth, life, death, and after his death, until his resurrection.

title: Westminster Larger Catechism — Q. 47
snippet: How did Christ humble himself in his conception and birth?
body: Christ humbled himself in his conception and birth, in that, being from all eternity the Son of God, in the bosom of the Father, he was pleased in the fullness of time to become the son of man, made of a woman of low estate, and to be born of her; with divers circumstances of mor…

title: Westminster Larger Catechism — Q. 48
snippet: How did Christ humble himself in his life?
body: Christ humbled himself in his life, by subjecting himself to the law, which he perfectly fulfilled; and by conflicting with the indignities of the world, temptations of Satan, and infirmities in his flesh, whether common to the nature of man, or particularly accompanying that his…

title: Westminster Larger Catechism — Q. 49
snippet: How did Christ humble himself in his death?
body: Christ humbled himself in his death, in that having been betrayed by Judas, forsaken by his disciples, scorned and rejected by the world, condemned by Pilate, and tormented by his persecutors; having also conflicted with the terrors of death, and the powers of darkness, felt and …

title: Westminster Larger Catechism — Q. 50
snippet: Wherein consisted Christ's humiliation after his death?
body: Christ's humiliation after his death consisted in his being buried; and continuing in the state of the dead and under the power of death till the third day, which hath been otherwise expressed in these words, He descended into hell.

title: Westminster Larger Catechism — Q. 51
snippet: What was the estate of Christ's exaltation?
body: The estate of Christ's exaltation comprehendeth his resurrection, ascension, sitting at the right hand of the Father, and his coming again to judge the world.

title: Westminster Larger Catechism — Q. 52
snippet: How was Christ exalted in his resurrection?

title: Westminster Larger Catechism — Q. 53
snippet: How was Christ exalted in his ascension?
body: Christ was exalted in his ascension, in that having after his resurrection often appeared unto and conversed with his apostles, speaking to them of the things pertaining to the kingdom of God, and giving them commission to preach the gospel to all nations, forty days after his re…

title: Westminster Larger Catechism — Q. 54
snippet: How is Christ exalted in his sitting at the right hand of God?
body: Christ is exalted in his sitting at the right hand of God, in that as God-man he is advanced to the highest favor with God the Father, with all fullness of joy, glory, and power over all things in heaven and earth; and doth gather and defend his Church, and subdue their enemies; …

title: Westminster Larger Catechism — Q. 55
snippet: How doth Christ make intercession?
body: Christ maketh intercession, by his appearing in our nature continually before the Father in heaven, in the merit of his obedience and sacrifice on earth, declaring his will to have it applied to all believers; answering all accusations against them, and procuring for them quiet o…

title: Westminster Larger Catechism — Q. 56
snippet: How is Christ to be exalted in his coming again to judge the world?
body: Christ is to be exalted in his coming again to judge the world, in that he, who was unjustly judged and condemned by wicked men, shall come again at the last day in great power, and in the full manifestation of his own glory and of his Father's, with all his holy angels, with a s…

title: Westminster Larger Catechism — Q. 57
snippet: What benefits hath Christ procured by his mediation?
body: Christ by his mediation hath procured redemption, with all other benefits of the covenant of grace.

title: Westminster Larger Catechism — Q. 58
snippet: How do we come to be made partakers of the benefits which Christ hath procured?
body: We are made partakers of the benefits which Christ hath procured by the application of them unto us, which is the work especially of God the Holy Ghost.

title: Westminster Larger Catechism — Q. 59
snippet: Who are made partakers of redemption through Christ?
body: Redemption is certainly applied, and effectually communicated, to all those for whom Christ hath purchased it; who are in time by the Holy Ghost enabled to believe in Christ according to the gospel.

title: Westminster Larger Catechism — Q. 60
snippet: Can they who have never heard of the gospel, and so know not Jesus Christ, nor believe in him, be saved by their living according to the light of nature?
body: They who, having never heard the gospel, know not Jesus Christ, and believe not in him, cannot be saved, be they never so diligent to frame their lives according to the light of nature, or the laws of that religion which they profess; neither is there salvation in any other, but …

title: Westminster Larger Catechism — Q. 61
snippet: Are all they saved who hear the gospel, and live in the Church?
body: All that hear the gospel, and live in the visible Church, are not saved; but only they who are true members of the Church invisible.

title: Westminster Larger Catechism — Q. 62
snippet: What is the visible Church?
body: The visible Church is a society made up of all such as in all ages and places of the world do profess the true religion, and of their children.

title: Westminster Larger Catechism — Q. 63
snippet: What are the special privileges of the visible Church?
body: The visible Church hath the privilege of being under God's special care and government; of being protected and preserved in all ages, notwithstanding the opposition of all enemies; and of enjoying the communion of saints, the ordinary means of salvation, and offers of grace by Ch…

title: Westminster Larger Catechism — Q. 64
snippet: What is the invisible Church?
body: The invisible Church is the whole number of the elect, that have been, are, or shall be gathered into one under Christ the head.

title: Westminster Larger Catechism — Q. 65
snippet: What special benefits do the members of the invisible Church enjoy by Christ?
body: The members of the invisible Church, by Christ, enjoy union and communion with him in grace and glory.

title: Westminster Larger Catechism — Q. 66
snippet: What is that union which the elect have with Christ?
body: The union which the elect have with Christ is the work of God's grace, whereby they are spiritually and mystically, yet really and inseparably, joined to Christ as their head and husband; which is done in their effectual calling.

title: Westminster Larger Catechism — Q. 67
snippet: What is effectual calling?
body: Effectual calling is the work of God's almighty power and grace, whereby (out of his free and special love to his elect, and from nothing in them moving him thereunto) he doth, in his accepted time, invite and draw them to Jesus Christ, by his Word and Spirit; savingly enlighteni…

title: Westminster Larger Catechism — Q. 68
snippet: Are the elect only effectually called?
body: All the elect, and they only, are effectually called; although others may be, and often are, outwardly called by the ministry of the Word, and have some common operations of the Spirit; who, for their willful neglect and contempt of the grace offered to them, being justly left in…

title: Westminster Larger Catechism — Q. 69
snippet: What is the communion in grace, which the members of the invisible Church have with Christ?
body: The communion in grace, which the members of the invisible Church have with Christ, is their partaking of the virtue of his mediation, in their justification, adoption, sanctification, and whatever else in this life manifests their union with him.

title: Westminster Larger Catechism — Q. 70
snippet: What is justification?

title: Westminster Larger Catechism — Q. 71
snippet: How is justification an act of God's free grace?
body: Although Christ, by his obedience and death, did make a proper, real and full satisfaction to God's justice in the behalf of them that are justified; yet in as much as God accepteth the satisfaction from a surety, which he might have demanded of them, and did provide this surety,…

title: Westminster Larger Catechism — Q. 72
snippet: What is justifying faith?
body: Justifying faith is a saving grace, wrought in the heart of a sinner, by the Spirit and Word of God, whereby he, being convinced of his sin and misery, and of the disability in himself and all other creatures to recover him out of his lost condition, not only assenteth to the tru…

title: Westminster Larger Catechism — Q. 73
snippet: How doth faith justify a sinner in the sight of God?
body: Faith justifies a sinner in the sight of God, not because of those other graces which do always accompany it, or of good works that are the fruits of it, nor as if the grace of faith, or any act thereof, were imputed to him for his justification; but only as it is an instrument b…

title: Westminster Larger Catechism — Q. 74
snippet: What is adoption?
body: Adoption is an act of the free grace of God, in and for his only Son Jesus Christ, whereby all those that are justified are received into the number of his children, have his name put upon them, the Spirit of his Son given to them, are under his fatherly care and dispensations, a…

title: Westminster Larger Catechism — Q. 75
snippet: What is sanctification?
body: Sanctification is a work of God's grace, whereby they whom God hath before the foundation of the world chosen to be holy, are in time through the powerful operation of his Spirit, applying the death and resurrection of Christ unto them, renewed in their whole man after the image …

title: Westminster Larger Catechism — Q. 76
snippet: What is repentance unto life?
body: Repentance unto life is a saving grace, wrought in the heart of a sinner by the Spirit and word of God, whereby, out of the sight and sense, not only of the danger, but also of the filthiness and odiousness of his sins, and upon the apprehension of God's mercy in Christ to such a…

title: Westminster Larger Catechism — Q. 77
snippet: Wherein do justification and sanctification differ?
body: Although sanctification be inseparably joined with justification, yet they differ, in that God in justification imputeth the righteousness of Christ; in sanctification his Spirit infuseth grace, and enableth to the exercise thereof; in the former, sin is pardoned; in the other, i…

title: Westminster Larger Catechism — Q. 78
snippet: Whence ariseth the imperfection of sanctification in believers?
body: The imperfection of sanctification in believers ariseth from the remnants of sin abiding in every part of them, and the perpetual lustings of the flesh against the spirit; whereby they are often foiled with temptations, and fall into many sins, are hindered in all their spiritual…

title: Westminster Larger Catechism — Q. 79
snippet: May not true believers, by reason of their imperfections, and the many temptations and sins they are overtaken with, fall away from the state of grace?
body: True believers, by reason of the unchangeable love of God, and his decree and covenant to give them perseverance, their inseparable union with Christ, his continual intercession for them, and the Spirit and seed of God abiding in them, can neither totally nor finally fall away fr…

title: Westminster Larger Catechism — Q. 80
snippet: Can true believers be infallibly assured that they are in the estate of grace, and that they shall persevere therein unto salvation?
body: Such as truly believe in Christ, and endeavor to walk in all good conscience before him, may, without extraordinary revelation, by faith grounded upon the truth of God's promises, and by the Spirit enabling them to discern in themselves those graces to which the promises of life …

title: Westminster Larger Catechism — Q. 81
snippet: Are all true believers at all times assured of their present being in the estate of grace, and that they shall be saved?
body: Assurance of grace and salvation not being of the essence of faith, true believers may wait long before they obtain it; and, after the enjoyment thereof, may have it weakened and intermitted, through manifold distempers, sins, temptations, and desertions; yet are they never left …

title: Westminster Larger Catechism — Q. 82
snippet: What is the communion in glory which the members of the invisible Church have with Christ?
body: The communion in glory which the members of the invisible Church have with Christ, is in this life, immediately after death, and at last perfected at the resurrection and day of judgment.

title: Westminster Larger Catechism — Q. 83
snippet: What is the communion in glory with Christ which the members of the invisible Church enjoy in this life?
body: The members of the invisible Church have communicated to them in this life the first-fruits of glory with Christ, as they are members of him their head, and so in him are interested in that glory which he is fully possessed of; and, as an earnest thereof, enjoy the sense of God's…

title: Westminster Larger Catechism — Q. 84
snippet: Shall all men die?
body: Death being threatened as the wages of sin, it is appointed unto all men once to die; for that all have sinned.

title: Westminster Larger Catechism — Q. 85
snippet: Death, being the wages of sin, why are not the righteous delivered from death, seeing all their sins are forgiven in Christ?
body: The righteous shall be delivered from death itself at the last day, and even in death are delivered from the sting and curse of it; so that, although they die, yet it is out of God's love, to free them perfectly from sin and misery, and to make them capable of further communion w…

title: Westminster Larger Catechism — Q. 86
snippet: What is the communion in glory with Christ, which the members of the invisible Church enjoy immediately after death?
body: The communion in glory with Christ, which the members of the invisible Church enjoy immediately after death, is, in that their souls are then made perfect in holiness, and received into the highest heavens, where they behold the face of God in light and glory; waiting for the ful…

title: Westminster Larger Catechism — Q. 87
snippet: What are we to believe concerning the resurrection?
body: We are to believe, that, at the last day, there shall be a general resurrection of the dead, both of the just and unjust: when they that are then found alive shall in a moment be changed; and the selfsame bodies of the dead which are laid in the grave, being then again united to …

title: Westminster Larger Catechism — Q. 88
snippet: What shall immediately follow after the resurrection?
body: Immediately after the resurrection shall follow the general and final judgment of angels and men; the day and hour whereof no man knoweth, that all may watch and pray, and be ever ready for the coming of the Lord.

title: Westminster Larger Catechism — Q. 89
snippet: What shall be done to the wicked at the day of judgment?
body: At the day of judgment, the wicked shall be set on Christ's left hand, and, upon clear evidence and full conviction of their own consciences, shall have the fearful but just sentence of condemnation pronounced against them; and thereupon shall be cast out from the favorable prese…

title: Westminster Larger Catechism — Q. 90
snippet: What shall be done to the righteous at the day of judgment?
body: At the day of judgment, the righteous, being caught up to Christ in the clouds, shall be set on his right hand, and there openly acknowledged and acquitted, shall join with him in the judging of reprobate angels and men, and shall be received into heaven, where they shall be full…

title: Westminster Larger Catechism — Q. 91
snippet: What is the duty which God requireth of man?
body: The duty which God requireth of man is obedience to his revealed will.

title: Westminster Larger Catechism — Q. 92
snippet: What did God at first reveal unto man as the rule of his obedience?
body: The rule of obedience revealed to Adam in the estate of innocence, and to all mankind in him, beside a special command not to eat of the fruit of the tree of the knowledge of good and evil, was the moral law.

title: Westminster Larger Catechism — Q. 93
snippet: What is the moral law?
body: The moral law is the declaration of the will of God to mankind, directing and binding every one to personal, perfect, and perpetual conformity and obedience thereunto, in the frame and disposition of the whole man, soul and body, and in performance of all those duties of holiness…

title: Westminster Larger Catechism — Q. 94
snippet: Is there any use of the moral law to man since the fall?
body: Although no man, since the fall, can attain to righteousness and life by the moral law; yet there is great use thereof, as well common to all men, as peculiar either to the unregenerate, or the regenerate.

title: Westminster Larger Catechism — Q. 95
snippet: Of what use is the moral law to all men?
body: The moral law is of use to all men, to inform them of the holy nature and will of God, and of their duty, binding them to walk accordingly; to convince them of their disability to keep it, and of the sinful pollution of their nature, hearts, and lives; to humble them in the sense…

title: Westminster Larger Catechism — Q. 96
snippet: What particular use is there of the moral law to unregenerate men?
body: The moral law is of use to unregenerate men, to awaken their consciences to flee from wrath to come, and to drive them to Christ; or, upon their continuance in the estate and way of sin, to leave them inexcusable, and under the curse thereof.

title: Westminster Larger Catechism — Q. 97
snippet: What special use is there of the moral law to the regenerate?

title: Westminster Larger Catechism — Q. 98
snippet: Where is the moral law summarily comprehended?
body: The moral law is summarily comprehended in the ten commandments, which were delivered by the voice of God upon mount Sinai, and written by him in two tables of stone; and are recorded in the twentieth chapter of Exodus. The four first commandments containing our duty to God, and …

title: Westminster Larger Catechism — Q. 99
snippet: What rules are to be observed for the right understanding of the ten commandments?
body: For the right understanding of the ten commandments, these rules are to be observed: 1. That the law is perfect, and bindeth every one to full conformity in the whole man unto the righteousness thereof, and unto entire obedience for ever; so as to require the utmost perfection of…

title: Westminster Larger Catechism — Q. 100
snippet: What special things are we to consider in the ten commandments?
body: We are to consider in the ten commandments, the preface, the substance of the commandments themselves, and the several reasons annexed to some of them the more to enforce them.

title: Westminster Larger Catechism — Q. 101
snippet: What is the preface to the ten commandments?
body: The preface to the ten commandments is contained in these words, I am the Lord thy God, which have brought thee out of the land of Egypt, out of the house of bondage. Wherein God manifesteth his sovereignty, as being Jehovah, the eternal, immutable, and almighty God; having his b…

title: Westminster Larger Catechism — Q. 102
snippet: What is the sum of the four commandments which contain our duty to God?
body: The sum of the four commandments containing our duty to God, is, to love the Lord our God with all our heart, and with all our soul, and with all our strength, and with all our mind.

title: Westminster Larger Catechism — Q. 103
snippet: Which is the first commandment?
body: The first commandment is, Thou shalt have no other gods before me.

title: Westminster Larger Catechism — Q. 104
snippet: What are the duties required in the first commandment?
body: The duties required in the first commandment are, the knowing and acknowledging of God to be the only true God, and our God; and to worship and glorify him accordingly, by thinking, meditating, remembering, highly esteeming, honoring, adoring, choosing, loving, desiring, fearing …

title: Westminster Larger Catechism — Q. 105
snippet: What are the sins forbidden in the first commandment?
body: The sins forbidden in the first commandment are atheism, in denying, or not having a God; idolatry, in having or worshiping more gods than one, or any with, or instead of the true God; the not having and avouching him for God, and our God; the omission or neglect of any thing due…

title: Westminster Larger Catechism — Q. 106
snippet: What are we especially taught by these words (before me) in the first commandment?
body: These words (before me) or before my face, in the first commandment teach us that God who seeth all things, taketh special notice of, and is much displeased with, the sin of having any other god; that so it may be an argument to dissuade from it, and to aggravate it as a most imp…

title: Westminster Larger Catechism — Q. 107
snippet: Which is the second commandment?
body: The second commandment is, Thou shalt not make unto thee any graven image, or any likeness of anything that is in heaven above, or that is in the earth beneath, or that is in the water under the earth: thou shalt not bow down thyself to them, nor serve them: for I the Lord thy Go…

title: Westminster Larger Catechism — Q. 108
snippet: What are the duties required in the second commandment?
body: The duties required in the second commandment are, the receiving, observing, and keeping pure and entire, all such religious worship and ordinances as God hath instituted in his Word; particularly prayer and thanksgiving in the name of Christ; the reading, preaching, and hearing …

title: Westminster Larger Catechism — Q. 109
snippet: What are the sins forbidden in the second commandment?
body: The sins forbidden in the second commandment are, all devising, counselling, commanding, using, and anywise approving, any religious worship not instituted by God himself; tolerating a false religion; the making any representation of God, of all, or of any of the three Persons, e…

title: Westminster Larger Catechism — Q. 110
snippet: What are the reasons annexed to the second commandment, the more to enforce it?
body: The reasons annexed to the second commandment, the more to enforce it, contained in these words, For I the Lord thy God am a jealous God, visiting the iniquity of the fathers upon the children unto the third and fourth generation of them that hate me; and showing mercy unto thous…

title: Westminster Larger Catechism — Q. 111
snippet: Which is the third commandment?
body: The third commandment is, Thou shalt not take the name of the Lord thy God in vain: for the Lord will not hold him guiltless that taketh his name in vain.

title: Westminster Larger Catechism — Q. 112
snippet: What is required in the third commandment?
body: The third commandment requires, that the name of God, his titles, attributes, ordinances, the word, sacraments, prayer, oaths, vows, lots, his works, and whatsoever else there is whereby he makes himself known, be holily and reverently used in thought, meditation, word, and writi…

title: Westminster Larger Catechism — Q. 113
snippet: What are the sins forbidden in the third commandment?
body: The sins forbidden in the third commandment are, the not using of God's name as is required; and the abuse of it in an ignorant, vain, irreverent, profane, superstitious, or wicked mentioning or otherwise using his titles, attributes, ordinances, or works, by blasphemy, perjury; …

title: Westminster Larger Catechism — Q. 114
snippet: What reasons are annexed to the third commandment?
body: The reasons annexed to the third commandment, in these words, "The Lord thy God," and "for the Lord will not hold him guiltless that taketh his name in vain" are, because he is the Lord and our God, therefore his name is not to be profaned or any way abused by us; especially beca…

title: Westminster Larger Catechism — Q. 115
snippet: What is the fourth commandment?
body: The fourth commandment is, Remember the sabbath-day, to keep it holy. Six days shalt thou labor, and do all thy work; but the seventh day is the sabbath of the Lord thy God: in it thou shalt not do any work, thou, nor thy son, nor thy daughter, thy man-servant, nor thy maid-serva…

title: Westminster Larger Catechism — Q. 116
snippet: What is required in the fourth commandment?
body: The fourth commandment requireth of all men the sanctifying or keeping holy to God such set times as he hath appointed in his word, expressly one whole day in seven; which was the seventh from the beginning of the world to the resurrection of Christ, and the first day of the week…

title: Westminster Larger Catechism — Q. 117
snippet: How is the sabbath or the Lord's day to be sanctified?
body: The sabbath or Lord's day is to be sanctified by an holy resting all the day, not only from such works as are at all times sinful, but even from such worldly employments and recreations as are on other days lawful; and making it our delight to spend the whole time (except so much…

title: Westminster Larger Catechism — Q. 118
snippet: Why is the charge of keeping the sabbath more specially directed to governors of families and other superiors?
body: The charge of keeping the sabbath is more specially directed to governors of families and other superiors, because they are bound not only to keep it themselves, but to see that it be observed by all those that are under their charge; and because they are prone ofttimes to hinder…

title: Westminster Larger Catechism — Q. 119
snippet: What are the sins forbidden in the fourth commandment?
body: The sins forbidden in the fourth commandment are, all omissions of the duties required, all careless, negligent, and unprofitable performing of them, and being weary of them; all profaning the day by idleness, and doing that which is in itself sinful; and by all needless works, w…

title: Westminster Larger Catechism — Q. 120
snippet: What are the reasons annexed to the fourth commandment, the more to enforce it?
body: The reasons annexed to the fourth commandment, the more to enforce it, are taken from the equity of it, God allowing us six days of seven for our own affairs, and reserving but one for himself, in these words, six days shalt thou labor and do all thy work: from God's challenging …

title: Westminster Larger Catechism — Q. 121
snippet: Why is the word remember set in the beginning of the fourth commandment?
body: The word remember is set in the beginning of the fourth commandment, partly, because of the great benefit of remembering it, we being thereby helped in our preparation to keep it; and, in keeping it, better to keep all the rest of the commandments, and to continue a thankful reme…

title: Westminster Larger Catechism — Q. 122
snippet: What is the sum of the six commandments which contain our duty to man?
body: The sum of the six commandments which contain our duty to man, is, to love our neighbor as ourselves, and to do to others what we would have them to do to us.

title: Westminster Larger Catechism — Q. 123
snippet: Which is the fifth commandment?
body: The fifth commandment is, Honor thy father and thy mother: that thy days may be long upon the land which the Lord thy God giveth thee.

title: Westminster Larger Catechism — Q. 124
snippet: Who are meant by father and mother in the fifth commandment?
body: By father and mother, in the fifth commandment, are meant, not only natural parents, but all superiors in age and gifts; and especially such as, by God's ordinance, are over us in place of authority, whether in family, church, or commonwealth.

title: Westminster Larger Catechism — Q. 125
snippet: Why are superiors styled father and mother?
body: Superiors are styled father and mother, both to teach them in all duties towards their inferiors, like natural parents, to express love and tenderness to them, according to their several relations; and to work inferiors to a greater willingness and cheerfulness in performing thei…

title: Westminster Larger Catechism — Q. 126
snippet: What is the general scope of the fifth commandment?
body: The general scope of the fifth commandment is the performance of those duties which we mutually owe in our several relations, as inferiors, superiors, or equals.

title: Westminster Larger Catechism — Q. 127
snippet: What is the honor that inferiors owe to their superiors?
body: The honor which inferiors owe to their superiors is, all due reverence in heart, word, and behavior; prayer and thanksgiving for them; imitation of their virtues and graces; willing obedience to their lawful commands and counsels; due submission to their corrections; fidelity to,…

title: Westminster Larger Catechism — Q. 128
snippet: What are the sins of inferiors against their superiors?

title: Westminster Larger Catechism — Q. 129
snippet: What is required of superiors towards their inferiors?
body: It is required of superiors, according to that power they receive from God, and that relation wherein they stand, to love, pray for, and bless their inferiors; to instruct, counsel and admonish them; countenancing, commending, and rewarding such as do well; and discountenancing, …

title: Westminster Larger Catechism — Q. 130
snippet: What are the sins of superiors?
body: The sins of superiors are, besides the neglect of the duties required of them, an inordinate seeking of themselves, their own glory, ease, profit, or pleasure; commanding things unlawful, or not in the power of inferiors to perform; counseling, encouraging, or favoring them in th…

title: Westminster Larger Catechism — Q. 131
snippet: What are the duties of equals?
body: The duties of equals are, to regard the dignity and worth of each other, in giving honor to go one before another; and to rejoice in each other's gifts and advancement, as their own.

title: Westminster Larger Catechism — Q. 132
snippet: What are the sins of equals?
body: The sins of equals are, besides the neglect of the duties required, the undervaluing of the worth, envying the gifts, grieving at the advancement or prosperity one of another; and usurping pre-eminence one over another.

title: Westminster Larger Catechism — Q. 133
snippet: What is the reason annexed to the fifth commandment, the more to enforce it?
body: The reason annexed to the fifth commandment in these words, "that thy days may be long upon the land which the Lord thy God giveth thee," is an express promise of long life and prosperity, as far as it shall serve for God's glory and their own good, to all such as keep this comma…

title: Westminster Larger Catechism — Q. 134
snippet: Which is the sixth commandment?
body: The sixth commandment is, Thou shalt not kill.

title: Westminster Larger Catechism — Q. 135
snippet: What are the duties required in the sixth commandment?
body: The duties required in the sixth commandment are, all careful studies, and lawful endeavours, to preserve the life of ourselves and others by resisting all thoughts and purposes, subduing all passions, and avoiding all occasions, temptations, and practices, which tend to the unju…

title: Westminster Larger Catechism — Q. 136
snippet: What are the sins forbidden in the sixth commandment?
body: The sins forbidden in the sixth commandment are, all taking away the life of ourselves, or of others, except in case of public justice, lawful war, or necessary defence; the neglecting or withdrawing the lawful and necessary means of preservation of life; sinful anger, hatred, en…

title: Westminster Larger Catechism — Q. 137
snippet: Which is the seventh commandment?
body: The seventh commandment is, Thou shalt not commit adultery.

title: Westminster Larger Catechism — Q. 138
snippet: What are the duties required in the seventh commandment?
body: The duties required in the seventh commandment are, chastity in body, mind, affections, words, and behavior; and the preservation of it in ourselves and others; watchfulness over the eyes and all the senses; temperance, keeping of chaste company, modesty in apparel; marriage by t…

title: Westminster Larger Catechism — Q. 139
snippet: What are the sins forbidden in the seventh commandment?
body: The sins forbidden in the seventh commandment, besides the neglect of the duties required, are, adultery, fornication, rape, incest, sodomy, and all unnatural lusts; all unclean imaginations, thoughts, purposes, and affections; all corrupt or filthy communications, or listening t…

title: Westminster Larger Catechism — Q. 140
snippet: Which is the eighth commandment?
body: The eighth commandment is, Thou shalt not steal.

title: Westminster Larger Catechism — Q. 141
snippet: What are the duties required in the eighth commandment?
body: The duties required in the eighth commandment are, truth, faithfulness, and justice in contracts and commerce between man and man; rendering to every one his due; restitution of goods unlawfully detained from the right owners thereof; giving and lending freely, according to our a…

title: Westminster Larger Catechism — Q. 142
snippet: What are the sins forbidden in the eighth commandment?
body: The sins forbidden in the eighth commandment, besides the neglect of the duties required, are, theft, robbery, man-stealing, and receiving any thing that is stolen; fraudulent dealing; false weights and measures; removing landmarks; injustice and unfaithfulness in contracts betwe…

title: Westminster Larger Catechism — Q. 143
snippet: Which the ninth commandment?
body: The ninth commandment is, Thou shalt not bear false witness against thy neighbor.

title: Westminster Larger Catechism — Q. 144
snippet: What are the duties required in the ninth commandment?
body: The duties required in the ninth commandment are, the preserving and promoting of truth between man and man, and the good name of our neighbor, as well as our own: appearing and standing for the truth; and from the heart, sincerely, freely, clearly, and fully, speaking the truth,…

title: Westminster Larger Catechism — Q. 145
snippet: What are the sins forbidden in the ninth commandment?
body: The sins forbidden in the ninth commandment are, all prejudicing the truth, and the good name of our neighbors, as well as our own, especially in public judicature; giving false evidence; suborning false witnesses; wittingly appearing and pleading for an evil cause; out-facing an…

title: Westminster Larger Catechism — Q. 146
snippet: Which is the tenth commandment?
body: The tenth commandment is, Thou shalt not covet thy neighbor's house, thou shalt not covet thy neighbor's wife, nor his man-servant, nor his maid-servant, nor his ox, nor his ass, nor any thing that is thy neighbor's.

title: Westminster Larger Catechism — Q. 147
snippet: What are the duties required in the tenth commandment?
body: The duties required in the tenth commandment are, such a full contentment with our own condition, and such a charitable frame of the whole soul toward our neighbor, as that all our inward motions and affections touching him, tend unto, and further all that good which is his.

title: Westminster Larger Catechism — Q. 148
snippet: What are the sins forbidden in the tenth commandment?
body: The sins forbidden in the tenth commandment are, discontentment with our own estate; envying, and grieving at the good of our neighbor, together with all inordinate motions and affections to anything that is his.

title: Westminster Larger Catechism — Q. 149
snippet: Is any man able perfectly to keep the commandments of God?
body: No man is able, either of himself, or by any grace received in this life, perfectly to keep the commandments of God; but doth daily break them in thought, word, and deed.

title: Westminster Larger Catechism — Q. 150
snippet: Are all transgressions of the law of God equally heinous in themselves, and in the sight of God?
body: All transgressions of the law of God are not equally heinous; but some sins in themselves, and by reason of several aggravations, are more heinous in the sight of God than others.

title: Westminster Larger Catechism — Q. 151
snippet: What are those aggravations that make some sins more heinous than others?
body: Sins receive their aggravations, 1. From the persons offending: if they be of riper age, greater experience or grace, eminent for profession, gifts, place, office, guides to others, and whose example is likely to be followed by others. 2. From the parties offended: if immediately…

title: Westminster Larger Catechism — Q. 152
snippet: What doth every sin deserve at the hands of God?
body: Every sin, even the least, being against the sovereignty, goodness, and holiness of God, and against his righteous law, deserveth his wrath and curse, both in this life, and that which is to come; and cannot be expiated but by the blood of Christ.

title: Westminster Larger Catechism — Q. 153
snippet: What doth God require of us, that we may escape his wrath and curse due to us by reason of the transgression of the law?
body: That we may escape the wrath and curse of God due to us by reason of the transgression of the law, he requireth of us repentance toward God, and faith toward our Lord Jesus Christ, and the diligent use of the outward means whereby Christ communicates to us the benefits of his med…

title: Westminster Larger Catechism — Q. 154
snippet: What are the outward means whereby Christ communicates to us the benefits of his mediation?
body: The outward and ordinary means whereby Christ communicates to his church the benefits of his mediation, are all his ordinances; especially the Word, Sacraments, and prayer: all which are made effectual to the elect for their salvation.

title: Westminster Larger Catechism — Q. 155
snippet: How is the Word made effectual to salvation?
body: The Spirit of God maketh the reading, but especially the preaching of the Word, an effectual means of enlightening, convincing, and humbling sinners; of driving them out of themselves, and drawing them unto Christ; of conforming them to his image, and subduing them to his will; o…

title: Westminster Larger Catechism — Q. 156
snippet: Is the Word of God to be read by all?
body: Although all are not to be permitted to read the Word publicly to the congregation, yet all sorts of people are bound to read it apart by themselves, and with their families: to which end, the holy Scriptures are to be translated out of the original into vulgar languages.

title: Westminster Larger Catechism — Q. 157
snippet: How is the Word of God to be read?
body: The holy Scriptures are to be read with an high and reverent esteem of them; with a firm persuasion that they are the very Word of God; and that he only can enable us to understand them; with desire to know, believe, and obey, the will of God revealed in them; with diligence, and…

title: Westminster Larger Catechism — Q. 158
snippet: By whom is the Word of God to be preached?
body: The Word of God is to preached only by such as are sufficiently gifted, and also duly approved and called to that office.

title: Westminster Larger Catechism — Q. 159
snippet: How is the Word of God to be preached by those that are called thereunto?
body: They that are called to labor in the ministry of the Word are to preach sound doctrine, diligently, in season, and out of season; plainly, not in the enticing words of man's wisdom but in demonstration of the Spirit, and of power; faithfully, making known the whole counsel of God…

title: Westminster Larger Catechism — Q. 160
snippet: What is required of those that hear the Word preached?
body: It is required of those that hear the Word preached, that they attend upon it with diligence, preparation, and prayer; examine what they hear by the Scriptures; receive the truth with faith, love, meekness, and readiness of mind, as the Word of God; meditate, and confer of it; hi…

title: Westminster Larger Catechism — Q. 161
snippet: How do the Sacraments become effectual means of salvation?
body: The Sacraments become effectual means of salvation, not by any power in themselves, or any virtue derived from the piety or intention of him by whom they are administered; but only by the working of the Holy Ghost, and the blessing of Christ by whom they are instituted.

title: Westminster Larger Catechism — Q. 162
snippet: What is a Sacrament?
body: A Sacrament is an holy ordinance instituted by Christ in his Church, to signify, seal, and exhibit unto those that are within the covenant of grace, the benefits of his mediation; to strengthen and increase their faith, and all other graces; to oblige them to obedience; to testif…

title: Westminster Larger Catechism — Q. 163
snippet: What are the parts of a Sacrament?
body: The parts of a Sacrament are two: the one, an outward and sensible sign used according to Christ's own appointment; the other, an inward and spiritual grace thereby signified.

title: Westminster Larger Catechism — Q. 164
snippet: How many Sacraments hath Christ instituted in his Church under the New Testament?
body: Under the New Testament Christ hath instituted in his Church only two Sacraments, Baptism and the Lord's Supper.

title: Westminster Larger Catechism — Q. 165
snippet: What is Baptism?
body: Baptism is a Sacrament of the New Testament, wherein Christ hath ordained the washing with water in the name of the Father, and of the Son, and of the Holy Ghost, to be a sign and seal of ingrafting into himself, of remission of sins by his blood, and regeneration by his Spirit; …

title: Westminster Larger Catechism — Q. 166
snippet: Unto whom is Baptism to be administered?
body: Baptism is not to be administered to any that are out of the visible Church, and so strangers from the covenant of promise, till they profess their faith in Christ, and obedience to him; but infants descended from parents, either both or but one of them professing faith in Christ…

title: Westminster Larger Catechism — Q. 167
snippet: How is our Baptism to be improved by us?
body: The needful but much neglected duty of improving our Baptism, is to be performed by us all our life long, especially in the time of temptation, and when we are present at the administration of it to others, by serious and thankful consideration of the nature of it, and of the end…

title: Westminster Larger Catechism — Q. 168
snippet: What is the Lord's Supper?
body: The Lord's Supper is a Sacrament of the New Testament, wherein, by giving and receiving bread and wine according to the appointment of Jesus Christ, his death is shewed forth; and they that worthily communicate feed upon his body and blood, to their spiritual nourishment and grow…

title: Westminster Larger Catechism — Q. 169
snippet: How hath Christ appointed bread and wine to be given and received in the Sacrament of the Lord's Supper?
body: Christ hath appointed the ministers of his Word, in the administration of this Sacrament of the Lord's Supper, to set apart the bread and wine from common use, by the word of institution, thanksgiving, and prayer; to take and break the bread, and to give both the bread and the wi…

title: Westminster Larger Catechism — Q. 170
snippet: How do they that worthily communicate in the Lord's Supper feed upon the body and blood of Christ therein?
body: As the body and blood of Christ are not corporally or carnally present in, with, or under the bread and wine in the Lord's Supper; and yet are spiritually present to the faith of the receiver, no less truly and really than the elements themselves are to their outward senses; so t…

title: Westminster Larger Catechism — Q. 171
snippet: How are they that receive the Sacrament of the Lord's Supper to prepare themselves before they come unto it?
body: They that receive the Sacrament of the Lord's Supper, are, before they come, to prepare themselves thereunto, by examining themselves of their being in Christ; of their sins and wants; of the truth and measure of their knowledge, faith, repentance, love to God and the brethren, c…

title: Westminster Larger Catechism — Q. 172
snippet: May one who doubteth of his being in Christ, or of his due preparation, come to the Lord's Supper?
body: One who doubteth of his being in Christ, or of his due preparation to the Sacrament of the Lord's Supper, may have true interest in Christ, though he be not yet assured thereof; and in God's account hath it, if he be duly affected with the apprehension of the want of it, and unfe…

title: Westminster Larger Catechism — Q. 173
snippet: May any who profess the faith, and desire to come to the Lord's Supper, be kept from it?
body: Such as are found to be ignorant or scandalous, notwithstanding their profession of the faith, and desire to come to the Lord's Supper, may and ought to be kept from that Sacrament, by the power which Christ hath left in his Church, until they receive instruction, and manifest th…

title: Westminster Larger Catechism — Q. 174
snippet: What is required of them that receive the Sacrament of the Lord's Supper in the time of the administration of it?
body: It is required of them that receive the Sacrament of the Lord's Supper, that, during the time of the administration of it, with all holy reverence and attention they wait upon God in that ordinance, diligently observe the sacramental elements and actions, heedfully discern the Lo…

title: Westminster Larger Catechism — Q. 175
snippet: What is the duty of Christians, after they have received the Sacrament of the Lord's Supper?
body: The duty of Christians, after they have received the Sacrament of the Lord's Supper, is seriously to consider how they have behaved themselves therein, and with what success; if they find quickening and comfort, to bless God for it, beg the continuance of it, watch against relaps…

title: Westminster Larger Catechism — Q. 176
snippet: Wherein do the Sacraments of Baptism and the Lord's Supper agree?
body: The Sacraments of Baptism and the Lord's Supper agree, in that the author of both is God; the spiritual part of both is Christ and his benefits; both are seals of the same covenant, are to be dispensed by ministers of the gospel and by none other; and to be continued in the Churc…

title: Westminster Larger Catechism — Q. 177
snippet: Wherein do the Sacraments of Baptism and the Lord's Supper differ?
body: The Sacraments of Baptism and the Lord's Supper differ, in that Baptism is to be administered but once, with water, to be a sign and seal of our regeneration and ingrafting into Christ, and that even to infants; whereas the Lord's Supper is to be administered often, in the elemen…

title: Westminster Larger Catechism — Q. 178
snippet: What is prayer?
body: Prayer is an offering up of our desires unto God, in the name of Christ, by the help of his Spirit; with confession of our sins, and thankful acknowledgment of his mercies.

title: Westminster Larger Catechism — Q. 179
snippet: Are we to pray unto God only?
body: God only being able to search the hearts, hear the requests, pardon the sins, and fulfill the desires of all; and only to be believed in, and worshiped with religious worship; prayer, which is a special part thereof, is to be made by all to him alone, and to none other.

title: Westminster Larger Catechism — Q. 180
snippet: What is it to pray in the name of Christ?
body: To pray in the name of Christ is, in obedience to his command, and in confidence on his promises, to ask mercy for his sake; not by bare mentioning of his name, but by drawing our encouragement to pray, and our boldness, strength, and hope of acceptance in prayer, from Christ and…

title: Westminster Larger Catechism — Q. 181
snippet: Why are we to pray in the name of Christ?
body: The sinfulness of man, and his distance from God by reason thereof, being so great, as that we can have no access into his presence without a mediator; and there being none in heaven or earth appointed to, or fit for, that glorious work but Christ alone, we are to pray in no othe…

title: Westminster Larger Catechism — Q. 182
snippet: How doth the Spirit help us to pray?
body: We not knowing what to pray for as we ought, the Spirit helpeth our infirmities, by enabling us to understand both for whom, and what, and how prayer is to be made; and by working and quickening in our hearts (although not in all persons, nor at all times, in the same measure) th…

title: Westminster Larger Catechism — Q. 183
snippet: For whom are we to pray?
body: We are to pray for the whole church of Christ upon earth; for magistrates and ministers; for ourselves, our brethren, yea, our enemies; and for all sorts of men living, or that shall live hereafter; but not for the dead, nor for those that are known to have sinned the sin unto de…

title: Westminster Larger Catechism — Q. 184
snippet: For what things are we to pray?
body: We are to pray for all things tending to the glory of God, the welfare of the church, our own or others' good; but not for any thing that is unlawful.

title: Westminster Larger Catechism — Q. 185
snippet: How are we to pray?
body: We are to pray with an awful apprehension of the majesty of God, and deep sense of our unworthiness, necessities, and sins; with penitent, thankful, and enlarged hearts; with understanding, faith, sincerity, fervency, love, and perseverance, waiting upon him, with humble submissi…

title: Westminster Larger Catechism — Q. 186
snippet: What rule hath God given for our direction in the duty of prayer?
body: The whole Word of God is of use to direct us in the duty of prayer; but the special rule of direction is that form of prayer which our Saviour Christ taught his disciples, commonly called, The Lord's Prayer.

title: Westminster Larger Catechism — Q. 187
snippet: How is the Lord's Prayer to be used?
body: The Lord's Prayer is not only for direction, as a pattern, according to which we are to make other prayers; but may also be used as a prayer, so that it be done with understanding, faith, reverence, and other graces necessary to the right performance of the duty of prayer.

title: Westminster Larger Catechism — Q. 188
snippet: Of how many parts doth the Lord's prayer consist?
body: The Lord's prayer consists of three parts; a preface, petitions, and a conclusion.

title: Westminster Larger Catechism — Q. 189
snippet: What doth the preface of the Lord's prayer teach us?
body: The preface of the Lord's prayer (contained in these words, Our Father which art in heaven,) teacheth us, when we pray, to draw near to God with confidence of his fatherly goodness, and our interest therein; with reverence, and all other child-like dispositions, heavenly affectio…

title: Westminster Larger Catechism — Q. 190
snippet: What do we pray for in the first petition?
